title: Predictive Fidelity Runtime Calibration — Product Brief
author: Samantha Ortiz
body:
Overview:

This brief describes the Predictive Fidelity Runtime Calibration (PFRC) product: an automated system that continuously calibrates per-tenant and per-route fidelity settings at runtime to meet customer SLOs (latency and cost targets) while preserving observed quality metrics. PFRC is a product- and runtime-level capability that complements Redwood Optimize; it operates as a low-latency controller in the serving runtime and as a telemetry+decision service in the control plane.

Goals:
- Reduce aggregate token cost for customers by 8–20% on latency-sensitive conversational workloads without degrading quality by >2% on tracked eval prompts.
- Keep 99th-percentile latency within configured SLOs for routes configured with latency budgets (target: 95% of requests under budget).
- Provide transparent, auditable adjustments (what changed, why, and the measured downstream impact).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: conversational and transactional text generation routes, session-aware workloads, route-level and tenant-level calibration policies, telemetry hooks, and rollout tooling.
- Out of scope: offline batch embedding pipelines, marketplace model licensing changes, or radical model switching (PFRC uses compatible variants/quantized versions, not new architectures).

Key concepts and definitions:
- Fidelity profile: a named set of runtime knobs (quantization level, KV-cache prefetch policy, max_decode_length, sampling temperature floor, prompt truncation heuristic).
- Calibration window: rolling 5-minute window used by the runtime controller to compute recent cost/latency/quality signals (configurable; defaults to 5 minutes).
- Adjustment: a single change to a route’s active fidelity profile (e.g., reduce quantization from 8-bit to 4-bit variant, or enable prefix caching).

Telemetry and signals used:
1) Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) — from serving runtime tracing.
2) Cost-per-token and cost-per-request — from token accounting.
3) Shadow-eval quality delta — lightweight fidelity-sensitive promptset runs captured on a sample of requests (example: 200 prompts/minute per tenant cap).
4) User-perceived fallbacks — measured via fallback counters and error-rate deltas.

SLOs and thresholds (default):
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Calibration action threshold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| p95 latency | <= 400 ms | p95 > 600 ms consistently 3 windows | p95 > 500 ms (start mitigations) |
| Cost per token | minimize | n/a | cost increase > 15% vs baseline after change |
| Eval quality delta | <= 2% absolute loss | > 3% | >= 2.5% (revert/attenuate) |

Controller design (high level):
- Runtime controller: A lightweight agent colocated with the serving shard. Maintains a sliding window of request signals, applies conservative heuristics to make fast, reversible adjustments (aim for sub-1s decision latency). Only applies adjustments that map to pre-certified fidelity profiles.
- Calibration decision service: A control-plane service that consumes aggregated telemetry, runs predictive models (time-series forecasting of latency and cost under candidate profiles) and recommends parameterized policies. It also stores the audit log for every adjustment and computes impact estimates used in rollout decisions.

Calibration algorithm summary:
1) Observe recent signals (latency, cost, shadow-eval quality).
2) Predict short-term latency/cost under each candidate profile using an ensemble: (a) linear transfer function tuned per-model and per-sequence-length, (b) small amortized ML model trained on historical traces.
3) Score candidates with a loss that weights latency-SLO violations and quality delta (default: latency weight 0.6, quality weight 0.4).
4) Select lowest-loss candidate that is allowed by policy and that has been certified for this tenant.
5) Apply adjustment with a conservative ramp: 10% of traffic -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 15 minutes subject to fast rollback triggers.

Policy and safety guardrails:
- Certification: Only profiles that passed the tenant’s preflight (quality regression test set) and the platform’s regression lab may be applied automatically.
- Traffic cap: PFRC will not change more than two knobs concurrently and will cap maximal per-route change frequency (default: 1 adjustment per 10 minutes).
- Fast rollback triggers: if p95 latency increases by >20% or eval quality delta exceeds 2.5% within 10 minutes of a ramp step, the runtime controller immediately reverts to the last known-good profile and flags the event.

Operational runbook (summary):
1) Preflight: product/onboarding must upload a tenant-specific fidelity testset and set target SLOs via the Console or onboarding API.
2) Activation: enable PFRC for the route with deployment policy (automatic | manual-review | off).
3) Monitoring: the Console shows a Calibration panel with current profile, recent adjustments, impact estimates, and audit trail links.
4) Incident (if rollback occurs):
   1. Oncall reviews the audit log at /console/calibrations/{tenant}/{route}.
   2. If the regression is platform-level, disable PFRC at the tenant scope and open an incident.
   3. If tenant-level, contact the customer success owner and schedule a follow-up evaluation.

Rollout plan and timeline (proposed):
- Q3 2026 (alpha): internal-only runs with Redwood product teams; limited to non-critical routes.
- Q4 2026 (beta): invite-only external customers, manual-review mode.
- Q1 2027 (general availability): automatic mode with default conservative policies.

Owner and stakeholders:
- Product lead: Samantha Ortiz (owner)
- Engineering: Runtime team (primary), Optimize team (secondary predictive models), Observability team (telemetry hooks)
- Customer success: Tier-1 CSMs for beta customers
- Security/compliance: sign-off required for any tenant-sensitive telemetry retention changes

Console UX and API surface changes:
- New Console panel: Calibration -> Live Recommendations. Shows: current profile, active adjustments (with % traffic), predicted impact graphs, and audit trail.
- Admin API endpoints (examples):
  - GET /v1/calibration/{tenant}/{route}  # returns active profile and audit pointers
  - POST /v1/calibration/{tenant}/{route}/activate {"mode":"automatic" | "manual-review"}  # enable PFRC
  - POST /v1/calibration/{tenant}/{route}/block {"profile":"4bit-quantized-v2"}  # prevent specific profile

Example runtime config (JSON-like example shown as CLI snippet):
```
redwood config set calibration --tenant=acme --route=/v1/chat --mode=automatic --slo-p95-ms=400 --quality-budget=2.0
```

Telemetry quotas and costs:
- Shadow-eval traffic capped at default 200 prompts/min/tenant. Additional shadow-eval capacity can be purchased (see pricing add-on section).
- Aggregated telemetry retention: default 90 days for calibration signals; extended retention requires opt-in with legal approval for customer data retention.

Pricing and packaging notes (product thinking):
- Basic: PFRC read-only recommendations included for all paying tenants (console visibility, manual-review activation).
- Advanced (add-on): automatic runtime adjustments, extended shadow-eval quota, and longer telemetry retention for a per-tenant monthly fee.
- Enterprise: SLA-backed calibration SLAs (e.g., guaranteed p95 latency under PFRC-managed routes) and professional services for certification and testset tuning.

Success metrics and measurement plan:
- Primary KPIs: average cost-per-request reduction, number of SLO violations prevented, percent of tenants who migrate to automatic mode within 90 days.
- Measurement cadence: weekly cohort analysis comparing beta tenants with matched controls, and daily short-term monitoring for regressions.

Open questions and risks:
- Can we maintain low false-positive rollback rates while being aggressive enough to capture cost savings? (risk: oscillation/repeated rollbacks)
- How to expose sufficient transparency to customers without overwhelming them with telemetry?
- Shadow-eval cost vs. value tradeoff for small tenants.

Appendix A — Example audit log entry (single-line example):
2026-05-20T14:03:22Z | tenant=acme | route=/v1/chat | from=full-precision | to=4bit-quantized-v2 | traffic=10% -> 30% | predicted_p95_ms=480 -> 360 | predicted_quality_delta=0.8% | decision_model_version=2026-05-12-v3

Appendix B — Acceptance criteria for GA:
- End-to-end e2e tests for at-rest and in-flight rollback must pass in staging for 95% of test workloads.
- No customer-facing regressions observed in alpha customers for a continuous 30-day window.
- Console audit and reporting panels are implemented and tested with synthetic data.

Contact and next steps:
- For product questions: Samantha Ortiz (samantha.ortiz@redwood.ai)
- To request inclusion in beta: open a ticket in Jira under PROJ-PFRC-beta and tag @product-onboarding.

This brief is intended to give stakeholders a single-page reference for scope, architecture, telemetry, rollout, and commercial thinking driving PFRC. Detailed design specs and the calibration decision-service API will be published as companion documents in product-docs/design-specs and product-docs/requirements.
